purpose: How an office coffee and water service operator measures what each stop on the route actually earns once product cost, service minutes and drive time are charged against it, diagnoses whether a weak stop is failing on consumption volume or on service time, reprices consumables honestly when supplier costs move, holds accounts through reliability and run-out prevention rather than through lock-in, and grows the book by expanding only into categories a measured account will genuinely pull - while keeping route density, obligation classes and concentration risk in view.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the operator runs an established office coffee and water service with placed equipment and a recurring consumables route, so the accounts discussed here are already installed and being served

every money quantity in this KB - stop contribution, markup, delivery minimum, credit, book value - is a mechanism the operator computes from their own delivery tickets, supplier invoices and route timings, never a market figure quoted from memory or an industry rule of thumb

service minutes, drive minutes and product draw are all measurable by the operator at ordinary effort; where they are not being measured, the first work is to start measuring rather than to estimate harder

food handling, sanitation, potable-water, weights-and-measures and unattended-retail obligations differ by jurisdiction and change over time; each appears here as an obligation class to verify with the responsible authority, never as a stated requirement
retention is earned by reliability and honest pricing; contractual lock-in is treated as a weak substitute that hides a failing stop rather than fixing it
exclusions: office segmentation, prospecting, tasting and free-trial acquisition plays, proposal design and the place-versus-rent-versus-sell decision for a new account - the market targeting and account acquisition KB owns all of it

brewer and water-system model selection, physical placement, water-line and drainage work, sanitation execution, consumables catalog construction, par-level mechanics, stockroom and van inventory, and the design of the route schedule and cleaning cadence - owned by the equipment placement and route logistics KB

invented specific figures of any kind: no stated per-cup prices, markup percentages, contribution margins, churn rates, spoilage rates, route-day stop counts or account-book multiples; every such quantity appears only as a mechanism for computing it from the operator's own records

assertions about what any specific food-handling, sanitation, backflow, weights-and-measures or unattended-retail rule requires in a named jurisdiction; obligation classes are named and flagged for local verification instead
personalized legal, tax, accounting, financial or insurance advice, and the drafting or interpretation of any specific service agreement, lease or asset-purchase contract
claims about the health effects of tap water, filtration, caffeine or any beverage, and every fear-based retention or expansion tactic built on such claims

pressuring an account into inventory it does not consume, stealth pack-size reduction, undisclosed surcharges, and any repricing move the operator would not be willing to state plainly to the client in writing

competency_questions.question: Which stops on my route actually make money once product cost, service minutes and drive time are charged against them, and which ones are being carried by the rest of the route?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STOP_ECONOMIC_UNIT fixes the stop as the unit of account and STOP_CONTRIBUTION_MECHANISM states the full chain from delivered product and price down to a per-stop contribution, with every input traceable to the operator's own tickets and timings

competency_questions.question: How do I measure what an account really draws and how long it really takes to serve, instead of guessing from the invoice total?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONSUMPTION_DRAW_MEASUREMENT defines per-visit draw capture and separates true draw from shrink and waste, and SERVICE_TIME_LEDGER defines park-to-park minute capture including building access and paperwork time

competency_questions.question: This stop is thin - is the problem too little consumption or too much service time, and which fix does that diagnosis license?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WEAK_STOP_DIAGNOSIS forks the stop on volume versus time using measured inputs and names the distinct remedy set each branch allows, and COST_TO_SERVE_DRIVERS supplies the driver list the time branch is tested against

competency_questions.question: How is the price this account pays actually composed, and can I explain every part of it out loud without embarrassment?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRICE_ARCHITECTURE decomposes the account price into product, equipment carry, service and any surcharge components and requires each component to be disclosable and defensible to the client

competency_questions.question: My supplier raised what I pay - how do I decide between absorbing it and passing it through, and how do I run the increase honestly?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COST_PASSTHROUGH_MECHANISM traces a documented input-cost move to the affected line and HONEST_REPRICE_PLAY specifies the notice, evidence, alternatives and no-stealth-shrinkflation conditions the increase must satisfy

competency_questions.question: How do I keep small accounts viable without punishing them with hidden fees or quietly padding their invoices?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DELIVERY_MINIMUM_DESIGN states the disclosed minimum-and-cadence instruments that make a small stop pay and CONCESSION_AND_CREDIT_DISCIPLINE bounds what may be given away and requires every concession to be recorded against the stop it burdens

competency_questions.question: What does a run-out actually cost me, and how do I prevent one without burying the client in inventory they resent?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STOCKOUT_INCIDENT_ECONOMICS converts a run-out into its retention and recovery cost and drives a root-caused prevention loop, while HONEST_EXPANSION_GATE and SERVICE_PROMISE_CAPACITY forbid solving it by overstocking the client or by promising a cadence the route cannot hold

competency_questions.question: How do I see an account leaving before the cancellation call comes?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ACCOUNT_HEALTH_SIGNALS lists the observable leading indicators drawn from draw, service and billing records with the review that acts on them, and CHAMPION_CONTINUITY covers the contact-loss case that hides the other signals

competency_questions.question: A brewer is down or an order arrived wrong - what recovery restores trust, and what should that recovery be allowed to cost?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SERVICE_RECOVERY_LOOP defines the acknowledge-restore-verify sequence with an interim-service option and CONCESSION_AND_CREDIT_DISCIPLINE prices the credit against the stop's own contribution

competency_questions.question: When should I fight to save an account, and when do I exit cleanly, recover my equipment and free the route minutes?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CHURN_DECISION_AND_EXIT states the save-versus-release test against measured contribution and route capacity and specifies the equipment recovery and handover conduct of an honest exit

competency_questions.question: Which of my accounts are genuinely ready for water service, snacks, breakroom supplies or a micro-market, and how do I offer it without overstocking them?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HONEST_EXPANSION_GATE requires measured pull and disclosed terms before any category is added, EXPANSION_CATEGORY_SCREEN compares candidate categories on margin, spoilage, shrink and added service minutes, and MICRO_MARKET_CLASS_UPGRADE states the qualification test for the unattended-retail class

competency_questions.question: What new obligation classes do I trigger when I add food, refrigeration, or an unattended self-checkout market to an account?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FOOD_HANDLING_OBLIGATION_SHIFT names the obligation classes that change at each expansion step and requires written local verification with the responsible authority before the category goes live

competency_questions.question: Should I take this new stop, and what is my route and account book actually worth if I ever sell it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ROUTE_DENSITY_AND_MARGINAL_STOP states the incremental-minutes test for adding a stop and BOOK_VALUE_AND_CONCENTRATION describes book value as a mechanism built from recurring contribution quality, transferability, equipment condition and concentration rather than as any quoted multiple

competency_questions.question: On what cadence do I re-run stop economics, and what do I do with the stops the review flags?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ROUTE_ECONOMICS_REVIEW fixes the review cycle, its inputs and the triage decision each flagged stop receives, and routes each decision to the pricing, retention, expansion or exit node that owns it

glossary.definition: One scheduled service visit to one account location: the atomic unit this KB measures money and minutes against, since two accounts in one building served on one visit are one stop, and one account with two floors served separately is two.
One driver-and-van day covering a sequenced loop of stops; its total minutes are the scarce resource that every added stop, extended service call and emergency response competes for.
The quantity of product an account actually consumes in a period, measured as what left the stockroom or cabinet between visits rather than what was ordered or invoiced.

Product that leaves the account without being consumed on site - single-serve pods pocketed for home use, snacks taken without payment in an unattended market - which inflates apparent draw and quietly destroys the margin the draw seems to promise.

What a single stop leaves behind after its own product cost, its service labor at a loaded rate, its share of drive time and its equipment carry are charged against its billed revenue; the number that decides whether a stop is grown, repriced, re-cadenced or released.

The full recurring cost of keeping one account served - service minutes, drive allocation, cleaning and sanitation labor, consumable freight, equipment maintenance and any building-access overhead - as distinct from the cost of the product itself.

The account running out of a core consumable between visits, forcing staff to buy retail or go without; the single most common trigger of avoidable churn in office coffee service and the event whose root cause the retention loop exists to eliminate.

A pre-portioned fractional package of ground coffee sized for one brew cycle; its yield per pack is what converts a cup-level consumption estimate into the unit count that appears on a delivery ticket.

A plumbed, filtered water dispenser that replaces delivered bottles; it shifts the account's recurring line from bottle deliveries to filter changes and sanitization visits, changing both the revenue shape and the service-minute shape of the stop.

An unattended self-checkout breakroom store with open racks, coolers and a payment kiosk; a distinct service class from coffee service because it introduces inventory shrink, date-coded perishable stock, planogram maintenance and a different set of local obligations.
